critical_steps: The source proof defines the perturbation energy with the square of the perturbing operator norm.
The source then needs that perturbation energy to be strictly below the original lower frame bound.
A singleton scalar example satisfies the printed unsquared condition and cancels the frame exactly.
The corrected strict threshold gives an explicit positive lower frame bound and is attained by the cancellation example.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact scalar cancellation plus a reverse-triangle analysis-operator estimate.
integrity.unproved_limits: No necessity claim is made beyond sharpness of the universal norm-only threshold.

scientific_limitations: The corrected threshold is a sharp universal sufficient norm condition, not a necessary condition for every particular perturbation direction.
The Hilbert-C*-module repair assumes the analysis operator is adjointable as in the source framework.
The finding is confined to the stated perturbation theorem and its direct later generalization.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A missing norm square invalidates an integral \(K\)-operator-frame perturbation theorem
